steps.title: Start one circle
steps.instruction: Type this small working example. Run it before adding more.
steps.explain: dot() draws a filled circle centered on the turtle. Its first input is the diameter: the full width across the circle.
steps.expected: The first visible part of the circle. This practice example tests the drawing code you will use next.
steps.question: What changes if you double the diameter?
steps.answer: The circle becomes twice as wide and twice as tall. Its center stays in the same place.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

steps.title: Name the circle code
steps.instruction: Replace the tested example with this function and its call. Keep the call at the left edge.
steps.explain: def disc(x, y, r, shade) names the code you tested. Its inputs replace the fixed values. The call underneath supplies those values and runs the indented body.
steps.expected: The practice shape should still appear. This step includes both the definition and a call.
steps.question: What would happen if you removed the disc(...) call at the bottom?
steps.answer: The function would be stored, but this example would no longer draw. A definition only runs when it is called.
steps.help: End the def line with a colon. Indent the body four spaces and a nested loop another four spaces. Put the call at the left edge.

steps.title: Test one repeat
steps.instruction: Build one example using the value shown. Run and inspect it.
steps.explain: i has one value in this test. Follow how it controls the drawing before putting the commands in a loop.
steps.expected: One visible example from the group. Check its position, size, and color.
steps.question: Where is i used in the drawing code?
steps.answer: Find the variable in the movement, size, or color expressions. A different value changes those instructions.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

lines: disc(math.cos(a) * r, math.sin(a) * r, sizes[i], shades[i])

steps.title: Make a second example
steps.instruction: Add a second example. Look for the lines you repeated.
steps.explain: Both examples use the same drawing instructions. Only an input value changes. You can put that repeated work in a loop.
steps.expected: Two examples from the group. Compare their positions or sizes.
steps.question: Which lines are identical in both examples?
steps.answer: The drawing instructions match. A loop can reuse them for each value.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

lines: disc(math.cos(a) * r, math.sin(a) * r, sizes[i], shades[i])

steps.title: Repeat the whole group
steps.instruction: Replace the trial examples with this loop. Run the whole program again.
steps.explain: for i in range(8): takes one value at a time. Indent the repeated body four spaces. The first line after the loop returns to the left edge.
steps.expected: The complete group. Compare it with the first example you tested.
steps.question: What changes if the loop has fewer values?
steps.answer: The body runs fewer times. range(n) supplies n values, starting at 0.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

lines: disc(math.cos(a) * r, math.sin(a) * r, sizes[i], shades[i])

steps.title: Check the complete drawing
steps.instruction: Run the completed program. Compare its shapes and details with the finished example.
steps.explain: The complete program combines the pieces you have tested, in drawing order.
steps.expected: An orbital map with planets at distinct distances

steps.nav: Make a change and explain it
steps.title: Make a change and explain it
steps.instruction: Choose one input in a function call or loop. Predict its effect, change it, and run. Then try a second change.
steps.explain: Change one thing at a time so you can connect the result to the exact line you edited.
steps.expected: Your own version of Solar System Diagram.
steps.question: Which line changed your drawing, and why?
steps.answer: Point to your edit, name the input you changed, and compare the result before and after.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.
